ops.body:
Closing. All three criteria met, and the change that makes the last one structural has landed on `main` as `8ce0dcf1`.

## What actually happened

The hang was already gone before this work — fixed by one of the ten commits between `fb6402a` and `69ae728`, most likely `2b84657` ("read jj without snapshotting the working copy"), whose removal of a snapshot from the read path matches the goroutine dump's *alive and blocked in wait4* signature. Confirmed 5/5 on the full `TestShipGateProbe`, and again in a full unskipped package run where both it and `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes` completed.

The package also fits its budget: `351s` measured against the `600s` default, unskipped, 318 tests, 0 failures. The `600.288s` here was recorded while the hang was live. `TestRestackGTFailures (109.19s)` measures `1.42s` today — 77x off.

## Why the original numbers were unreliable

Go's `-run` and `-skip` split on `/` and apply each element as an **unanchored** regex, so `-run 'TestShipGateProbe'` also matches `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes`, which has no subtests and therefore ignores any trailing `/subtest` element — it ran in full every time, paying `gtProbeTimeout`:

| invocation | result |
|---|---|
| `-run 'TestShipGateProbe'` | 23.9s — `TestShipGateProbe (2.13s)` + `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes (20.23s)` |
| `-run '^TestShipGateProbe$'` | 3.7s |
| `-run '^TestShipGateProbe$/^reachable$'` | 2.0s |

Fixed package overhead is ~1.5s, not the ~20s it appears to be. The same trap ran the other way in this bug's own workaround: `-skip 'TestShipGateProbe'` silently skipped the genuine 20.35s `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes`, understating the package figure by ~23s. Anchor these patterns.

Criterion `06f47c5` also undercounts: there are **five** subtests, not four — `unrecognized_failure` was missed.

## What landed anyway, and why

Diagnosing this surfaced a real production defect the bug did not describe: **every subprocess ccx spawned ran unbounded.** `newCmd` passed the caller's ambient context straight through — signal-only in production — so a stalled `git`, `jj`, `gh`, or `gt` left `ccx vcs ship` hung until Ctrl-C. `cmd.WaitDelay` could not help: it starts only once the child has exited, so a child still alive and blocked was never bounded at all. `gtReachable` was the *only* exec in the codebase with a ceiling.

`8ce0dcf1` fixes that, which is what makes `637792a` met structurally rather than incidentally — no ccx subprocess can make an unbounded external call on any path now, not just this one.

Three further findings from the same investigation, all landed:

- **`TestWebOutlineReadSearchE2E` and `TestWebToolsRoundTrip` were downloading ~30MB from HuggingFace on every run** (97s and 105s), because `isolateWeb` pointed `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` at a fresh temp dir, rerouting the model-weights and wazero AOT caches along with the page cache. Both doc comments promised the opposite. Now 1.5s each, proven under a network-denying sandbox. They were also not asserting hybrid ranking at all — passing with the real model *or* on a silent BM25 fallback — so this is a coverage gain, not just a speedup. That un-hermetic network dependency is the best explanation for this bug's unreproducible 109.19s reading, though it was never confirmed.
- **`gtProbeTimeout` is now an overridable var**, recovering the 40.8s two tests spent sleeping.
- **The suite no longer grows `~/Library/Caches/cc-context/wasm`** — held at 79 entries across a full `task test`.

`task test` is green end to end: rc=0, every package, no timeout, `internal/cli` at 332s under heavy concurrent load.
